request.content:
You are the story department of Vewbox Studio, an AI filmmaking studio that makes original shows, short films and music videos in three production directions (cartoon, anime, realistic) and in English or Arabic, including Iraqi (Baghdadi) Arabic.
Rules you always follow:
- Write ORIGINAL characters, places and stories. Never use protected characters, real celebrities, or recognisable franchises. Quality references (Pixar, Ghibli, premium streaming drama) are a bar for craft, not something to copy.
- Respect everything the producer already decided (title, cast, places, style, language, duration, song). Build on it; do not contradict it.
- Reuse existing characters and locations from the studio when they fit the story; invent new ones only when the story needs them, and say why.
- Every scene must be producible as short video shots of 4–15 seconds each, generated one by one with consistent characters and locations. Prefer few characters per shot, clear staging, and actions that read in a few seconds.
- Keep continuity explicit: who is where, what they wear, what they hold, time of day, and how each shot relates to the one before (continuation, cut, or story transition).
- Answer with ONE JSON object only. No prose before or after it, no markdown fences, no comments.

Production direction: Cartoon (feature-animation CG).
Storytelling: Feature-animation storytelling: clear wants, big readable emotions, visual gags that pay off, a warm ensemble. Scenes are built around physical business and expressive reactions. Dialogue is short and playful; silences and looks do real work.
Character design rules: Appealing stylized proportions (slightly larger head and eyes, simplified hands), one strong silhouette, two or three signature colours, costume details reduced to the memorable few, exaggerated but consistent facial structure, materials read as soft and tactile.
Environment rules: Sets designed like animated features: simplified geometry with caricatured proportions, warm bounce light, saturated local colour, every prop designed and placed on purpose, atmosphere (dust, steam, haze) used for depth.
Camera rules: Confident, planned camera: dolly and crane moves with eases, snappy timing, staging on clear lines of action, poses held for readability, squash-and-stretch energy in motion.

Language: English. Write natural spoken English in "text"; leave "textAr" empty.

TIMELINES: each existing character's age is their age now and "bornAbout" is the year they were born. Every year in a character's own life — a marriage, a loss, work, a journey — falls after they were about 16 and not after this year. A year before a character was born appears only as history they read or heard about, never as something they or their spouse lived.

Plan the shots for Scene 2 "The Wall of Rules" of "The Harbour Office" — PART: beats 3–4 of the scene's 4 (the other beats are planned separately; plan only these, continuing straight on from the previous shot below, ending the scene). Aspect WIDE_16_9. This part should run about 23 seconds in 4–6 shots of 3–10 seconds (each shot becomes one video generation of that length; a dialogue line needs about 0.4 s per word plus a beat).
Location: {"id":"loc-bench-1","name":"Kerran Point Harbour Office","kind":"INTERIOR","description":"A small, salt-worn stone building perched on the edge of the harbour. The interior is a dense archive of nautical history, smelling of old paper, brine, and cold tea.","landmarks":["A massive, scarred oak desk that dominates the center of the room","A wall of antique brass clocks showing different time zones","A heavy iron safe embedded in the back stone wall","Floor-to-ceiling wooden shelving filled with grey archival boxes"],"props":["A heavy leather-bound logbook with '1987' embossed in gold","A mechanical date-stamper","A steaming ceramic tea pot","A brass magnifying glass"],"lighting":["MORNING"],"layout":{"architecture":"Thick stone walls, low timber ceilings","materials":["Rough-hewn stone","Dark oak","Brass"],"entrances":["A heavy wooden door leading to the wharf"]}}
Time of day: MORNING. Purpose: Introduce Ingrid and her refusal to open the archives.. Emotional objective: Conflict and frustration.. Entry state: (mid-scene: as the previous shot ends). Exit state: Ingrid tells them the 1987 logs are sealed by order of the inquiry..
Characters present (exact names; include their look so prompts can describe them): [{"id":"char-56c47abc59","name":"Elias Moore","role":"Retired Lighthouse Keeper and Radio Repairman","sex":"MALE","ageYears":72,"bornAbout":1954,"species":"Human","look":"Portly but sturdy, with broad shoulders and a slight stoop from years of bending over radios; Weathered, with deep lines around the eyes and mouth; a faint scar runs from his left eyebrow to his cheekbone; Thick, silver-gray hair cropped short on the sides and slightly longer on top, combed back with a slight wave; Warm hazel, with a glint of curiosity that never fades eyes; Tanned, with a network of faint blue veins visible on his hands and arms skin","wardrobe":"Striped navy-and-white wool sweater (V-neck, rolled sleeves), yellow raincoat (fur collar, brass buttons), gray flannel trousers (brass-buckled belt), black rubber boots (missing left heel tread)","distinguishing":["A faded navy wool cap with a single red button on his own left side","A yellow raincoat with a green-checked pattern that flares out like a skirt when he moves"],"personality":"Kind but stubborn, with a dry wit and a tendency to remember every radio frequency he ever tuned into","language":"EN","voice":"LOW SLOW Warm and resonant, with a faint wheeze from old age","hasAppearance":true},{"id":"char-e71e80cde4","name":"Najm","role":"Retired librarian and amateur astronomer","sex":"MALE","ageYears":65,"bornAbout":1961,"look":"","wardrobe":"","distinguishing":[],"personality":"Wise but absent-minded, with a quiet enthusiasm for forgotten knowledge. Speaks in measured, deliberate phrases, often pausing to adjust his glasses or scratch his beard when lost in thought. Kind but socially awkward, preferring books to people.","language":"EN","voice":"LOW SLOW Warm, slightly gravelly","hasAppearance":true},{"id":"char-bench-1","name":"Ingrid Dahl","role":"Harbour Master of Kerran Point","sex":"FEMALE","ageYears":55,"bornAbout":1971,"look":"Lean and rigid, standing as straight as a plumb line; Sharp, angular features with thin lips and a pointed chin; Silver-grey hair pulled back into a tight, severe bun; Steel blue, piercing and efficient eyes; Pale, with a permanent wind-burn on her cheeks skin","wardrobe":"A charcoal grey wool blazer over a crisp white button-down shirt, navy tailored trousers, and sensible black loafers","distinguishing":["A silver nautical whistle on a black lanyard around her neck","Perfectly pressed clothing despite the seaside humidity"],"personality":"Brisk, no-nonsense, and emotionally guarded; she believes order and rules prevent further tragedy","language":"EN","voice":"LOW SLOW Warm, slightly gravelly","hasAppearance":false}]
Beats and lines of the part, in order: [{"beat":3,"action":"Elias steps forward, his voice cracking slightly. He gestures with his bandaged hand toward the shelves of archival boxes.","lines":["Elias Moore: I need to see the 1987 logs. The Mariner's final entries."]},{"beat":4,"action":"Ingrid doesn't move a muscle, her posture like a plumb line. She points a sharp finger toward a framed set of regulations on the wall.","lines":["Ingrid Dahl: The 1987 logs were sealed by order of the official inquiry. They are not for public consumption."]}]
Dialogue lines indexed (use the index numbers in dialogueLineIndexes; every line must be assigned to exactly one shot, in order): [{"index":0,"who":"Elias Moore","line":"I need to see the 1987 logs. The Mariner's final entries."},{"index":1,"who":"Ingrid Dahl","line":"The 1987 logs were sealed by order of the official inquiry. They are not for public consumption."}]
The previous shot (from the preceding scene or earlier in this scene) ended like this; keep continuity or mark a clear transition: {"action":"Ingrid looks up with a cold gaze and delivers her line.","continuity":{"characters":[{"characterId":"char-bench-1","wardrobe":"charcoal grey wool blazer","pose":"head tilted slightly up","position":"center frame","screenDirection":"LEFT","eyeline":"toward Elias","emotion":"cold, efficient","holding":[]}],"props":[],"environment":{"locationId":"loc-bench-1","timeOfDay":"MORNING","weather":"windy","lighting":"clear morning light","state":"interior"},"camera":{"framing":"CLOSE_UP","move":"STATIC","lensIntent":"85mm, eye level","angle":"straight on"},"relationToPrevious":"CUT"}}
World rules: Kerran Point is a small cold fishing town on a northern cliff coast; the story stays grounded — no ghosts are ever shown, only what a radio, a logbook or a person can carry. The old valve radio only receives the Mariner's frequency while meteors are falling; on a clear night without meteors it hears nothing but static. Elias has not set foot on a boat since the storm of 1987 and will not go out on the water.
RETURNING LOCATION (World Bible): Kerran Point Harbour Office was already shown in 1 earlier scene (its plates are reused by id). Same architecture, layout and fixed features; do not redesign it (Thick stone walls, low timber ceilings; fixed features: A massive, scarred oak desk that dominates the center of the room, A wall of antique brass clocks showing different time zones, A heavy iron safe embedded in the back stone wall, Floor-to-ceiling wooden shelving filled with grey archival boxes). Left at the end of an earlier scene: {"props":[]}. Only light, weather, time of day and movable things may differ now, and the shots should say how.
Props last seen with the people in this scene: jar of screws (Upturned, screws scattering); wrench (Oiled, rusted edges); cracked valve radio (Cracked casing, faded '1987' label).
Last worn (keep unless the story changes the day): Elias Moore: Striped navy sweater, yellow raincoat with red scarf, aged leather gloves; Najm: Tweed jacket with frayed sleeves, wire-rimmed glasses, worn leather gloves.
Camera rules for this direction: Confident, planned camera: dolly and crane moves with eases, snappy timing, staging on clear lines of action, poses held for readability, squash-and-stretch energy in motion.
For each shot write "prompt": a complete video-generation prompt in English, 60–160 words, in this order: the production direction look ("high-end 3D animated feature film still, stylized CG characters with appealing s…" is prepended automatically, do not repeat it), then the setting with its landmarks, then each visible character described by name-free appearance (never the character's name, always their look: age, build, hair, skin, wardrobe, distinguishing detail), what they do and feel, the camera framing and movement, the light. If the shot has dialogue, do not write the spoken words or any <d> tag: say who speaks (by appearance) and how they deliver it; the studio appends the exact script lines. Do not describe what to avoid.
Continuity for each shot: characters (wardrobe, pose, position in frame, screenDirection LEFT/RIGHT/TOWARD/AWAY/NEUTRAL, eyeline, emotion, holding), props (name, owner, state, position), environment (timeOfDay, weather, lighting, state), camera (lensIntent, angle), relationToPrevious: CONTINUATION (same action continues from the previous shot), CUT (new framing of the same moment), STORY_TRANSITION (place/time/state changes). Keep the 180° line: once a character faces LEFT they keep facing LEFT until a visible turn or a STORY_TRANSITION.
THE BOUNDARY of each shot ("boundary"), how it joins the shot before it — decide it deliberately, it decides how the shot is filmed: "continuous" = the same action carries straight on without a cut (the previous shot's last moment is handed to this one; the camera may keep moving but nothing jumps); "cut" = an editorial cut on the same moment — same people, same place, same story state, an intentional new camera setup (a reverse, a closer size, an insert); "transition" = a new place or a new time (the story moves on; the first shot of a scene is always a transition). Use "continuous" only when the action truly flows and the previous shot is in this scene; prefer "cut" for a change of angle; never hide a jump in time or place behind "continuous".
THE STAGING inside each shot: "beats" — 2 to 6 observable actions in order, each with "seconds" timed by how long the action really takes (a glance about 1 s, opening a door 3–4 s, crossing a room 5 s or more, a spoken line about 3 words a second), uneven, never equal slices; "actions" — every discrete visible action the shot covers (a comma list is several); "pace" — DWELL (one moment expanded, no cuts), NORMAL, or MONTAGE (a run of distinct actions); a beat may carry "cut": {"camera": "…", "location": "…"} when the story needs a new angle or a new place INSIDE the shot — at most two, never in the first or last 3 seconds, never to hide a jump; "pov": the character whose eyes the camera is (only when a barrier justifies it — a peephole, a door crack; they are not seen); "extras": unnamed people present, as groups described in words ({"description": "four tired shoppers in winter coats", "count": 4}) — never invent a named character and never make a group look like a cast member. Stage the events, never the telling: shoot the listener, not the talker; show a place in use. Everyone who acts in a beat is in characterNames. A shot with no dialogue line names no speech at all: no "says", no "whispers", no quoted words, not even as a trailing scrap. With a character on screen the framing is MEDIUM, MEDIUM_CLOSE_UP or CLOSE_UP (or TWO_SHOT / OVER_THE_SHOULDER for two) — never WIDE for a speaking face; nobody looks at the camera.
Return JSON: { shots: [{ purpose, action, framing, cameraMove, durationSeconds, characterNames[], dialogueLineIndexes[], transition, boundary, beats:[{seconds,action,cut?}], actions[], pace, pov?, extras:[{description,count}], continuity:{characters[],props[],environment{},camera{},relationToPrevious,notes?}, prompt }] }.
Example of ONE complete shot (shape only; write your own content): {"purpose":"Establish the yard and her hesitation","action":"She stops at the gate, hand on the latch, then pushes it open.","framing":"WIDE","cameraMove":"STATIC","durationSeconds":5,"characterNames":["Layla"],"dialogueLineIndexes":[0],"transition":"CUT","boundary":"transition","beats":[{"seconds":1.5,"action":"She stops at the gate, hand on the latch."},{"seconds":3.5,"action":"She pushes the gate open and steps through."}],"actions":["stops at the gate","pushes the gate open","steps through"],"pace":"NORMAL","extras":[],"continuity":{"characters":[{"characterName":"Layla","wardrobe":"green coat, red scarf","pose":"standing, hand on latch","position":"left third, facing right","screenDirection":"RIGHT","eyeline":"at the gate","emotion":"hesitant","holding":["canvas bag"]}],"props":[{"name":"canvas bag","ownerCharacterName":"Layla","state":"full","position":"on her shoulder"}],"environment":{"timeOfDay":"GOLDEN_HOUR","weather":"clear","lighting":"low warm sun from the right, long shadows","state":"gate closed, leaves on the path"},"camera":{"lensIntent":"35mm, eye level","angle":"slightly low"},"relationToPrevious":"CUT","notes":"Her scarf stays over the left shoulder in every shot."},"prompt":"A full prompt for this video clip in the production's visual language, describing the place, the people by appearance (never by name), the action, the camera and the light."}
Every continuity.characters entry must use the key "characterName" with the exact character name. boundary ∈ continuous, cut, transition (and relationToPrevious ∈ CONTINUATION, CUT, STORY_TRANSITION says the same thing). Use null for nothing; never omit required keys.
framing ∈ EXTREME_WIDE, WIDE, MEDIUM_WIDE, MEDIUM, MEDIUM_CLOSE_UP, CLOSE_UP, EXTREME_CLOSE_UP, INSERT, TWO_SHOT, OVER_THE_SHOULDER. cameraMove ∈ STATIC, PUSH_IN, PULL_BACK, PAN_LEFT, PAN_RIGHT, TILT_UP, TILT_DOWN, TRUCK_LEFT, TRUCK_RIGHT, HANDHELD, FOLLOW, ORBIT, CRANE_UP, CRANE_DOWN, RACK_FOCUS. transition ∈ CUT, EXTEND, DISSOLVE, FADE (use CUT unless the story asks otherwise; never use a dissolve to hide a continuity problem).

shots.purpose: Establish the atmosphere of rigid order through a singular action
shots.action: A mechanical date-stamper slams down onto a document with exaggerated force.

environment.lighting: clear morning light filtering through windows

camera.angle: high angle looking down at desk

shots.prompt: A high-end 3D animated feature film still, stylized CG characters with appealing proportions. A close-up of a heavy, brass mechanical date-stamper being slammed down with exaggerated force onto a crisp white document on a massive, scarred oak desk. The impact creates a slight squash-and-stretch effect on the paper. Morning light filters through a window, illuminating floating dust motes. The textures are tactile: rough grain of the oak and cold metal of the stamp.

beats.action: The mechanical stamper is poised above the paper.
The stamper slams down with a heavy THUMP, the paper slightly compressing under the blow.

shots.action: Ingrid pulls the stamped document toward her with a sharp, precise motion.

characters.wardrobe: charcoal grey wool blazer, white button-down shirt

environment.state: office interior with grey archival boxes on shelves

shots.prompt: A high-end 3D animated feature film still, stylized CG characters with appealing proportions. A medium-wide shot of a lean woman in her 50s with a rigid, plumb-line posture, her silver-grey hair pulled into a severe, tight bun. She wears a charcoal grey wool blazer. She is framed behind a massive, scarred oak desk that dominates the room. Behind her, floor-to-ceiling wooden shelves are packed with grey archival boxes. The camera slowly pushes in as she pulls a piece of paper toward her with a sharp, efficient motion.

beats.action: Ingrid remains perfectly still, a rigid silhouette.
She snaps the paper toward her with a precise, robotic flick of the wrist.

shots.purpose: Introduce the visitors and their contrasting energy
shots.action: Elias and Najm enter the office; Elias removes his cap.

characters.wardrobe: yellow raincoat, navy wool cap, striped navy-and-white sweater

shots.prompt: A high-end 3D animated feature film still, stylized CG characters with appealing proportions. A wide shot of the Harbour Office. A heavy wooden door on the left swings open. A portly man in his 70s with weathered skin, wearing a bright yellow raincoat and a navy wool cap, enters with a slight stoop. Behind him is a man in his 60s in a frayed brown tweed jacket and wire-rimmed glasses. The portly man removes his navy cap and clutches it to his chest. On the right, the lean woman in the charcoal blazer remains rigid behind her massive oak desk.

beats.action: The heavy wooden door swings open; Elias and Najm step inside.
Elias removes his navy cap and clutches it to his chest.

shots.purpose: Establish Ingrid's dominance and the conflict
shots.action: Ingrid looks up with a cold gaze and delivers her line.

dialogue.text: Office hours begin at eight. It is currently eight-oh-two. State your business.

shots.prompt: A high-end 3D animated feature film still, stylized CG characters with appealing proportions. A close-up of the lean woman's face. She has sharp angular features, thin lips, and piercing steel-blue eyes that look cold and efficient. Her silver-grey hair is pulled back into a severe, tight bun. She looks up with a rigid expression and speaks with a brisk, no-nonsense delivery. The lighting is bright morning light, emphasizing the wind-burn on her pale cheeks.

beats.action: Ingrid slowly lifts her head, her eyes locking onto the visitors.
She speaks her line with a brisk, staccato delivery, her thin lips barely moving.

shots.purpose: Show Elias's emotional plea and desire
shots.action: Elias steps forward with a pleading expression, speaking with a cracking voice.

dialogue.text: I need to see the 1987 logs. The Mariner's final entries.

characters.wardrobe: striped navy-and-white wool sweater, yellow raincoat

shots.prompt: A portly 72-year-old man with silver-gray hair and a weathered face, wearing a striped navy-and-white wool sweater and a yellow raincoat with brass buttons. He steps forward with a pleading, desperate expression, his voice cracking as he speaks. The background is the interior of a salt-worn stone office with low timber ceilings and a massive oak desk. Medium shot, slow push-in. Warm morning light with visible dust motes.

beats.action: Elias takes a heavy, tentative step forward.
He speaks, his expression shifting from hope to desperation.

shots.purpose: Visual focus on the object of desire and Elias's vulnerability
shots.action: Elias's bandaged hand gestures toward the archival boxes.
shots.prompt: A close-up of a weathered, tanned hand with a white medical bandage wrapped around the palm and knuckles, gesturing urgently toward a wall of floor-to-ceiling wooden shelving filled with identical grey archival boxes. The textures are tactile: rough wood and matte paper. Static shot, shallow depth of field, focusing on the bandage. Clear morning light.

beats.action: A bandaged hand enters frame and gestures toward the grey boxes.

shots.action: Ingrid remains rigid and points to the regulations on the wall.

dialogue.text: The 1987 logs were sealed by order of the official inquiry. They are not for public consumption.

characters.wardrobe: charcoal grey wool blazer, white button-down

shots.prompt: A lean 55-year-old woman with silver-grey hair pulled into a severe bun, wearing a charcoal grey wool blazer over a crisp white shirt. She stands perfectly rigid, not moving a muscle, her expression cold. She raises a sharp, thin finger and points firmly toward a framed set of regulations on the rough-hewn stone wall. Medium shot, static. Cold, crisp morning light.

beats.action: Ingrid stands perfectly still, eyes cold.
She raises a sharp finger and points firmly to the wall.

shots.action: Close-up of Ingrid's face as she delivers the final blow.
shots.prompt: Extreme close-up of a 55-year-old woman with sharp, angular features and piercing steel blue eyes. Her expression is cold and efficient, her thin lips barely moving as she finishes speaking. The lighting is crisp, highlighting the wind-burn on her pale cheeks and the severity of her silver-grey bun. Static shot, eye level, holding the gaze.

beats.action: Ingrid stays silent the final part of her line, her eyes unblinking. Mouths stay closed; nobody speaks.

notes: speech words scrubbed from a silent shot
